metadata.title: What Happens When Capgo is Unavailable
metadata.description: Understanding Capgo behavior when service is down, canceled, or when you exceed plan limits

blocks.text: What Happens When Capgo is Unavailable
Capgo is designed to be resilient and non-blocking. Your app continues to work even when Capgo services are temporarily unavailable. This document explains what happens in various scenarios.
If Capgo's servers are temporarily unavailable or experiencing an outage:
Your app continues to work normally
— Users can still open and use your app
— The automatic update check fails silently
No error is shown to users
— The update process gracefully fails in the background
— Any previously downloaded updates stay on the device
— Once service is restored, normal update behavior resumes
Capgo is designed with a "fail-safe" approach: if update services are unavailable, your app simply ignores the update and continues functioning normally.
Existing updates remain on user devices
— Users who already downloaded updates keep those versions
— The app stops checking for and downloading updates
— Your app continues to work without any changes
— Your dashboard and analytics data remains accessible for a period
— Resubscribing restores full update functionality immediately
The update mechanism gracefully degrades — your app becomes "static" but fully functional after cancellation.
When You Exceed Your Plan Limits
If you exceed your plan's MAU (Monthly Active Users), bandwidth, or storage limits:
New users may not receive updates
— The update check continues but may be throttled
— Users who already have updates continue using them
— New user tracking might be paused
— Users won't receive new updates until you add credits or upgrade
— Existing app version continues to work
— Update failures are silent and non-blocking
— You won't be able to upload new app versions
You can upgrade or add storage
— Resolving the limit restores full functionality
— Ensure core functionality works without updates
— Have a traditional app store update process as backup
— Keep track of usage to avoid unexpected behavior
— Verify your app behaves correctly when updates stop
